item.title: Logo and basic branding for FLOxford, Oxford's local free, libre, and open-source software group

item.content:encoded:
Organization: FLOxford

Status: filled

Compensation: paid

Role: Logo Design, Branding

About us

We’re FLOxford, a volunteer group holding talks and workshops about Free/Libre and Open-Source Software (FLOSS) in the city of Oxford, United Kingdom. These talks and workshops cover a range of technical and non-technical topics around FLOSS, from ethics to contributing in various ways, and we’ve also had several about the intersection of FLOSS and academia or research, because some of our members are University researchers or students. (Please note, however, that we are neither affiliated to a University nor exclusively focused on academia.) These events are usually open to all, recorded and streamed online where possible. Our group also has a social aspect, and will probably adopt other aspects in the future, for example visiting external FLOSS conferences as a group.

What we need

We have operated in the past, but without a name or brand identity. We plan to start our next season of events in October 2026, and introduce our brand alongside it. We already have the name FLOxford, but need a logo and branding for it; see the deliverables or email Oliver Geer on o@ogeer.org for more details.

Possible inspiration includes: our past talks and workshops, the Oxford Wikipedia article, and past event recordings. The design should be welcoming to both non-technical and technical people, not suggest any organisational affiliation (we are independent, at least right now), and link clearly to FLOSS and our local nature while not narrowing our possible activities.

Licensing of your contributions

We will assume your logo is Creative Commons Zero dedicated to the public domain, because attributing the logo every time it’s used isn’t feasible, and a brand requires a unique level of control by its represented organisation. I guess FLOxford will have unregistered trademark rights over it. That said, at our discretion and at least subject to our code of conduct, we can attribute you here on our website.

Your style guide document (and, if provided, the poster template), on the other hand, not extending to all designs we make using the style guide, can be licensed under any of the free culture licenses CC0, CC-BY-4.0, or CC-BY-SA-4.0.

Payment

We currently have no organisational funding except for our organisers’ pockets. I’d love to #PayForFreeSoftware and support Open Source Design, but if you’re unwilling to get paid less than or around £150, applying is probably a waste of time.

Email me (o@ogeer.org) with your ideas (as a few sentences; no visual design is needed in the first email since I might reject/suggest changes to your ideas) and the cost you are willing to work for before commencing work. I can pay via a bank transfer to the Single Euro Payments Area (which includes the European Union, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom), or by a PayPal transfer to anywhere.

I won’t pay for AI-generated logos; it feels unjust to pay someone for something that isn’t their work.

How to Apply:

  • o@ogeer.org

item.title: Monoshape logo - favicon ready

item.description: Clarity is a project that was neglected by me. I want to create a new website and need a logo that will look good on a favicon and represent the Monoshape icon theme. item.title: Create SVG graphics for wellness app
item.dc:creator: Web app for "Daily Wellness Empowerment Program"
item.description: Paul from mentalhealthrevolution.org has has developed the Daily Wellness Empowerment Program (DWEP) course. This has further been developed into an app with the help of a programmer (Tord) https://dwep-app.gitlab.io/ The DWEP app has 10 different practices, and we’d like to have SVG icons/graphics for each of these, possibly with a short animation of the SVG when pressing “done” for the practice Also we’d like to have SVG files for the states that each practice can be in: Done, Undetermined
item.content:encoded:
Organization: Web app for "Daily Wellness Empowerment Program"

Status: expired

Compensation: gratis

Role: Graphical design

Paul from mentalhealthrevolution.org has has developed the Daily Wellness Empowerment Program (DWEP) course. This has further been developed into an app with the help of a programmer (Tord) https://dwep-app.gitlab.io/

The DWEP app has 10 different practices, and we’d like to have SVG icons/graphics for each of these, possibly with a short animation of the SVG when pressing “done” for the practice

Also we’d like to have SVG files for the states that each practice can be in: Done, Undetermined

(We are also considering creating a new app logo)

item.title: Inkscape internship
item.dc:creator: Inkscape internship
item.description: ​Hi, I’m offering an internship position for a project focused on Inkscape. The internship will last 3 months full time, but can also be split in smaller part-time chucks. The workplace is a coworking space in the center of Bordeaux. People applying must have the following skills : Show a good knowledge of Inkscape interface and workflow Speak one of the following languages: English, French, Italian, Spanish, Catalan or Portuguese The main tasks will be creating flat designs, assets and isometric blocks using Inkscape. The laptop is not provided, so people should bring their own laptop and work with it, The total amount paid for the 3 months is around 1600€ net, which is the standard salary for internships here in France.
item.content:encoded:
Organization: Inkscape internship

Status: filled

Compensation: paid

Role: Inkscape, Vector, Design, Isometric

​Hi,

I’m offering an internship position for a project focused on Inkscape.

The internship will last 3 months full time, but can also be split in smaller part-time chucks. The workplace is a coworking space in the center of Bordeaux.

People applying must have the following skills :

  1. Show a good knowledge of Inkscape interface and workflow
  2. Speak one of the following languages: English, French, Italian, Spanish, Catalan or Portuguese
  • The main tasks will be creating flat designs, assets and isometric blocks using Inkscape.
  • The laptop is not provided, so people should bring their own laptop and work with it,

The total amount paid for the 3 months is around 1600€ net, which is the standard salary for internships here in France.

If you are interested in the position, please send your resume and any kind of support showing your Inkscape skills (portfolio, website) to the following address: fanialivio@gmail.com

No motivation letter required.

Livio

item.title: SVG Plant Icons
item.dc:creator: OpenFarm.cc, FarmBot.io, Hortomatic.com
item.description: Hi! My name is Rory and I founded two open-source projects. FarmBot is an open-source CNC farming machine and web app designed for small scale automated DIY precision farming. OpenFarm is a free and open database for farming and gardening knowledge. We’re starting to build a drag and drop farm designer/manager tool where one can graphically layout and keep track of plants on a map. Think: Farmville, but with utility! A core visual component of this will be crop icons that visually represent the plants. We want these icons to be usable across different projects, scalable, and beautiful. We have one contributor (@andru) who wants to contribute, and we would love more designers to help us out. We would host the icons on OpenFarm and they would all be licensed very permissively (CC0/MIT) and be avilable for download and via the OpenFarm API.
item.content:encoded:
Organization: OpenFarm.cc, FarmBot.io, Hortomatic.com

Status: filled

Compensation: gratis

Role: Icon Designer

Hi!

My name is Rory and I founded two open-source projects. FarmBot is an open-source CNC farming machine and web app designed for small scale automated DIY precision farming. OpenFarm is a free and open database for farming and gardening knowledge.

We’re starting to build a drag and drop farm designer/manager tool where one can graphically layout and keep track of plants on a map. Think: Farmville, but with utility! A core visual component of this will be crop icons that visually represent the plants. We want these icons to be usable across different projects, scalable, and beautiful. We have one contributor (@andru) who wants to contribute, and we would love more designers to help us out. We would host the icons on OpenFarm and they would all be licensed very permissively (CC0/MIT) and be avilable for download and via the OpenFarm API.

We’re having discussion about this here: https://github.com/openfarmcc/OpenFarm/issues/685. Please join in!

How to Apply:

Contact rory@openfarm.cc, roryaronson, http://slack.openfarm.cc
